# Choice of Law Dataverse (CoLD)

> An open, citable research database on choice of law in international commercial
> contracts. CoLD records how courts, legislators and arbitral institutions across
> more than 200 jurisdictions treat party autonomy — the freedom of contracting
> parties to choose the law governing their agreement. Content is licensed CC BY 4.0.

CoLD is built and maintained as an academic project funded by the Swiss National
Science Foundation. Every record is derived from a primary source: a court decision,
a statute, a convention, an arbitral award, or a published jurisdiction report.

Prefer the API over scraping HTML — it is public, unauthenticated for reads, returns
JSON, and is described by an OpenAPI document.

## Data

- [Court decisions](https://cold.global/court-decision): Judgments on choice of law, each with the facts, the choice of law issue, the court's position, and the relevant provisions
- [Jurisdiction reports](https://cold.global/jurisdiction/CHE): Per-country analysis of how a jurisdiction treats party autonomy, answering a common questionnaire
- [Domestic instruments](https://cold.global/domestic-instrument): National statutes and codifications, with HCCH Principles and UNCITRAL Model Law compatibility
- [Regional instruments](https://cold.global/regional-instrument): Regional conventions such as the Rome I Regulation and the Mexico Convention
- [International instruments](https://cold.global/international-instrument): Conventions and instruments including the HCCH Principles
- [Arbitral awards](https://cold.global/arbitral-award): Awards addressing the law applicable to the merits
- [Arbitral institutions](https://cold.global/arbitral-institution): Institutions, linked to their rules and awards
- [Arbitral rules](https://cold.global/arbitral-rule): Institutional rules and their choice of law provisions
- [Literature](https://cold.global/literature): Scholarly writing, indexed by jurisdiction and theme
- [Specialists](https://cold.global/specialist): Contributors of jurisdiction reports and expertise

## API

- [OpenAPI description](https://api.cold.global/api/v1/openapi.json): Machine-readable description of every endpoint
- [API reference](https://api.cold.global/api/v1/docs): Human-readable documentation
- [API catalog](https://cold.global/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 linkset pointing at the above
- [Sitemap index](https://cold.global/sitemap_index.xml): Every indexable URL, split by entity type

Useful endpoints, all `GET` and unauthenticated:

- `https://api.cold.global/api/v1/search/` — full-text search across all datasets
- `https://api.cold.global/api/v1/search/details?table={table}&id={coldId}` — a single record
- `https://api.cold.global/api/v1/entities/{slug}` — paginated lists; slugs are `court-decisions`, `jurisdictions`, `literature`, `domestic-instruments`, `regional-instruments`, `international-instruments`, `arbitral-awards`, `arbitral-institutions`, `arbitral-rules`, `specialists`, `questions`
- `https://api.cold.global/api/v1/statistics/counts` — record counts per entity type

## Understanding the data

- [Methodology](https://cold.global/learn/methodology): How jurisdictions are selected, how the questionnaire is framed, and how sources are coded
- [Glossary](https://cold.global/learn/glossary): Definitions of the private international law terms used throughout
- [FAQ](https://cold.global/learn/faq): What CoLD covers and how the data is produced
- [Data sets](https://cold.global/learn/data-sets): Bulk downloads
- [About](https://cold.global/about/about-cold): Project background and team

## Citation and reuse

Content is licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Reuse
requires attribution. Cite as: Choice of Law Dataverse <https://cold.global>

CoLD asks not to be used as training data for machine learning models; see
[robots.txt](https://cold.global/robots.txt), which sets `Content-Signal: ai-train=no`
and disallows training crawlers. Retrieving pages to answer a user's question is
welcome.
